questions.question: What is migration in human geography?
choices: Movement of people involving a change in usual residence
Any shipment of goods between ports
Only travel for a one-day holiday
Only changes in a city's street names

questions.question: What is immigration?
choices: Movement out of a country to live elsewhere
Movement of goods across a border
Movement into a country to live there
Movement between rooms in one home

questions.question: What is emigration?
choices: Movement into a country to live there
Movement out of a country to live elsewhere
A country's total number of births
A government's count of households

questions.question: What is internal migration?
choices: A move between two sovereign countries
A daily trip to work without changing residence
A shipment of products between factories
A residential move within the same country

questions.question: What is a push factor?
choices: A condition encouraging people to leave a place
A condition attracting people to a destination
A map's measure of elevation
An official count of imports

questions.question: What is a pull factor?
choices: A condition forcing every resident to emigrate
A change in a country's birth rate
A condition attracting people to a destination
The cost of printing travel documents

questions.question: What are remittances?
choices: Taxes paid only on imported vehicles
Money migrants send to people in their place of origin
Payments governments make to foreign armies
The total cost of building a highway

questions.question: Why can jobs influence migration?
choices: Employment has no relationship to residential decisions
Only retired people can migrate for economic reasons
Every migrant is guaranteed work on arrival
People may move toward employment or away from limited opportunities

questions.question: How can family networks affect migration?
choices: They may provide information, housing, and support for newcomers
They eliminate every legal and financial barrier
They require every family member to move at once
They prevent migrants from maintaining ties across borders

questions.question: Why can conflict cause forced displacement?
choices: Conflict automatically gives every person a new citizenship
Displacement occurs only after a formal peace treaty
Threats to safety may leave people with little practical choice about leaving
Only economic preferences can cause migration

questions.question: How does an internally displaced person differ from someone displaced across an international border?
choices: The internally displaced person necessarily has a new nationality
The internally displaced person remains within the same country
Cross-border movement always occurs for tourism
Internal displacement involves goods rather than people

questions.question: Why is it risky to assume every migrant moves for one reason?
choices: Every migration decision has an identical cause
All migrants move voluntarily without constraints
Destination conditions are never relevant
Economic, family, safety, environmental, and other factors can interact

questions.question: How can migration affect a destination's population?
choices: It can change size, age structure, skills, and cultural patterns
It changes only the number of buildings
It necessarily makes every resident the same age
It has no relationship to local services

questions.question: What challenge can origin communities face when many skilled workers leave?
choices: An automatic doubling of the trained workforce
The immediate end of all household income
Reduced availability of certain skills and services
The disappearance of every family connection

questions.question: Why can distance and cost affect migration patterns?
choices: Every destination costs the same to reach
They influence which destinations are accessible
Distance prevents all long-distance movement
Transportation costs are unrelated to decisions

questions.question: A family leaves an area because repeated crop failures threaten its livelihood. Which factor is most clearly illustrated?
choices: A destination pull factor
An increase in export prices alone
A decline in road traffic alone
A push factor

questions.question: A worker moves to a city after receiving a job offer. Which factor is most directly involved?
choices: A pull factor
A decline in natural increase
A change in latitude alone
A reduction in remittances

questions.question: A person leaves Country A and settles in Country B. How is the same move described?
choices: Immigration to A and emigration from B
Internal migration in both countries
Emigration from A and immigration to B
Natural population increase in both countries

questions.question: A person moves from a rural town to a city within the same nation. What type of migration is this?
choices: International immigration
Internal migration
International emigration
Cross-border displacement

questions.question: Why should a migration study compare origin and destination conditions?
choices: Only destination climate can influence movement
Origin communities experience no consequences
Migration patterns can be explained without geographic context
The decision and its effects involve both places
